title: Market Pulse
body_html:
This post reflects my current views on the market, sectors, and internal breadth/momentum. Expect candid, data-driven analysis, peppered with personal insights drawn from years of trading experience. I aim to provide value in every edition, helping you to see the market through a clearer, more informed lens.

What You Can Expect

  • In-Depth Market Analysis: A thorough examination of market trends, key indices, and pivotal turning points.

  • Sector Spotlights: A closer look at the hottest (and not-so-hot) sectors, highlighting opportunities and risks.

  • Breadth and Momentum Insights: Understanding the underlying strength of the market through breadth indicators and momentum metrics.

Exclusive Features

  • Interactive Spreadsheet: Alongside each post, I’ll be linking a detailed spreadsheet that tracks the breadth and momentum metrics. This will allow you to follow along with the data and see the trends I’m analyzing day-by-day.

  • Quick Video Commentary: To complement the metrics, I’ll also be posting a quick video commentary on most days. This will provide a more dynamic overview of the market, offering you additional context and clarity.

Market Metrics

Overall: Negative

The market remains in a weak technical position, with all four major indices still trading below their 10-, 20-, and 50-day moving averages. Until the major indices can reclaim these key levels and sustain buying pressure, the path of least resistance remains lower, with sellers likely to step in at overhead resistance. While large caps have managed to tilt breadth and momentum slightly toward the positive, mid- and small-cap stocks continue to lag, keeping overall market internals weak and limiting broad participation.

On the sector front, the market continues to be led by defensive names such as communication services, consumer defensive, and real estate, indicating that investors remain risk-averse. Meanwhile, growth-oriented sectors like technology and consumer cyclical are underperforming, sitting near the bottom of the relative strength rankings, further reinforcing the lack of risk appetite. Until the major indices reclaim key moving averages and internals improve across the board, this remains a defensive, risk-off market where caution is warranted.

Index Trends: Negative

Plan of Action

Stay Defensive and Avoid Aggressive Long Exposure

  • All four major indices remain below their 10-, 20-, and 50-day moving averages, confirming a continued downtrend.

  • The pace of downside expansion has slowed, but this is NOT bottom necessarily— just a temporary pause in selling and a bounce.

  • Large caps show slight improvement in breadth and momentum, but mid- and small caps remain weak.

  • Defensive sectors (communication services, consumer defensive, real estate) continue to lead, while growth-oriented sectors (technology, consumer cyclical) are still weak.

  • Lack of institutional risk appetite = no strong buying pressure.

  • Until major indices reclaim key moving averages and internals improve, the market remains unfavorable for long exposure.

  • Best approach: Stay defensive, limit risk, and focus on capital preservation.

Reduce Exposure and Remain Highly Selective

  • Exit or Reduce Weak Positions: Any long positions struggling to hold key support should be cut to avoid further downside risk.

  • Avoid Chasing Breakouts: Breakouts continue to fail, reinforcing the lack of quality setups in the current environment.

  • Only Consider Defensive Trades (If Trading at All): If engaging in trades, focus only on defensive sectors showing relative strength. Avoid risk-on sectors until institutions show renewed buying interest.

Monitor Market Internals for Signs of Stabilization

  • Breadth and Momentum Remain Weak: While selling pressure has slowed, internals are still negative, and the overall trend remains intact.

  • Watch for Signs of Selling Exhaustion: Key indicators of a potential shift in market direction include:

    • A slowdown in new lows

    • A contraction in downside momentum

    • Early signs of institutional buying

Until these factors start improving, the market remains vulnerable to further downside.

Stay Flexible and Proactively Manage Risk

  • Keep Cash Levels High: Cash remains the safest position in this environment. There is no reason to aggressively deploy capital until conditions improve.

  • Use Protective Stops on Any Remaining Positions: Given elevated volatility, tight stops should be in place to limit downside risk.

  • Do Not Try to Catch a Falling Market: Failed rebounds and false breakouts remain common. Avoid buying dips until a real shift in momentum is confirmed.

Reassess Market Conditions Daily

  • Evaluate Continuously: The market remains in a distribution phase, requiring daily reassessment of breadth, momentum, and sector strength.

  • Adapt Exposure Responsively: If selling pressure accelerates, reduce exposure even further. If internals start stabilizing and indices reclaim key levels, consider a cautious re-engagement with strict risk management.

Key Focus

  • Patience and Discipline: This is not a market for aggressive swing trading. Avoid forcing trades and wait for confirmation of improving conditions.

  • Look for Signs of a Turnaround: The key indicators for re-engagement include:

    • A slowdown in downside momentum

    • An improvement in breadth

    • An increase in new highs over new lows

  • Prepare for High Volatility: Continued selling pressure suggests ongoing market swings. Staying defensive and adaptable remains critical.

Bottom Line:

The market remains under heavy selling pressure, with only a slight slowdown in downside expansion. Internals are still weak, breadth and momentum remain negative, and all four major indices continue to trade below key moving averages.

This is not an environment for aggressive trading. The best approach remains staying on the sidelines or keeping exposure very light until conditions improve. Monitor internals for stabilization, track any shift in momentum, and only consider re-engagement when meaningful strength emerges.
